steps.step: 2a. Two-order relative entropy identity eq:phil-conditioned-event-information.
steps.reasoning: Let B=1_E, R_t=(X_t,S_t), joint law L on {0,1} x (R^12 x J), reference Bern(1-r) x mu with mu=mu_{T,p(t)}. Chain rule (lem:prob-kl-chain-rule, in [0,inf], no absolute-continuity hypothesis) with B first: KL(L||ref) = KL(Bern(1-r)||Bern(1-r)) + (1-r)KL(q_t^E||mu) + r KL(q_t^{E^c}||mu). With R_t first: KL(L||ref) = KL(q_t||mu) + E_{R_t}[KL(L(B|R_t)||Bern(1-r))] = KL(q_t||mu) + I(B;R_t), using that the B-marginal is exactly Bern(1-r). Both orders equal the same quantity, giving the displayed identity. I(B;R_t) <= H(B) = h_b(1-r) = h_b(r). KL(q_t||mu) <= eta by hypothesis (line 9), valid for t in [theta,2s] subset [s,2s]. Numerically verified on random discrete examples (check_kl.py, diff <= 1e-16), including I = h_b(r) equality when B is a function of R. The identity is pure measure theory and does not depend on E being a past event, so no conditioning-on-future issue arises; the reference uses the native deterministic rows p(t), consistent with the hypothesis (proof line 75-76 states this explicitly).

steps.step: 2b. Derivation of kappa_E, r=0 case, absolute continuity and finiteness.
steps.reasoning: Dropping r KL(q_t^{E^c}||mu) >= 0: (1-r)KL(q_t^E||mu) <= eta + h_b(r). Since r<=rho<1/2 and h_b is increasing on [0,1/2] (h_b'(r)=log((1-r)/r)>0; also checked numerically), h_b(r)<=h_b(rho); 1/(1-r)<=1/(1-rho). Hence KL(q_t^E||mu) <= (eta+h_b(rho))/(1-rho) = kappa_E. r=0: E has full probability, q_t^E=q_t, KL<=eta<=kappa_E, and h_b(0)=0 so the identity is the trivial one. Absolute continuity: q_t^E(A)=q_t(A cap E)/(1-r) <= q_t(A)/(1-r), and q_t << mu because KL(q_t||mu)<=eta<inf; finiteness of KL(q_t^E||mu) follows from the bound itself.

steps.reasoning: From def:rg-formation-cycle-experiment (c13:1188-1211): r^b_i = kbar_{i+1}-kbar_i-omega_i, r^m_i likewise, D_e = (1/2)[(r^b)^2+(r^m)^2], V_S = sum_i D_{e(i,S_i)}; for S^(0)=(1,0,3,2) both endpoints select e_0 and e_2 so V = 2D_{e_0}+2D_{e_2} and H_M = 2 sum_{g in {e,f}} (a^b_g a^b_g^T + a^m_g a^m_g^T) (ca_formation_proofs:1862-1863). Dx = kbar - mbar, R_ev = 2 D^T D = D^T D / v with v=1/2, Omega = I + R_ev, A_M = K_M = H_M + T Omega (ca_selection_proofs:14-16). Exact sympy computation (check_cycle.py): Gram(a^b,a^m) = [[3,1],[1,3]]; n^+_g=(a^b+a^m)/(2sqrt2), n^-_g=(a^b-a^m)/2 are unit and orthogonal; H_M n^+ = 8 n^+, H_M n^- = 4 n^-; R_ev n^+ = 0, R_ev n^- = 4 n^-; rank H_M = 4 (kernel dim 8). F_M = [(n^+_e-n^+_f)/sqrt2, n^-_e, n^-_f] has F^T F = I_3; F^T K_M F = diag(8+T,4+5T,4+5T); F^T (H_M+TI) F = diag(8+T,4+T,4+T); F^T R_ev F = diag(0,4,4). Block structure: P_W H_M P_Z = P_W R_ev P_Z = P_W K_M P_Z = 0 exactly, so K_M is block diagonal on W_M (+) Z_M. Hence under mu_{T,p} on sheet M, x ~ N(0,T K_M^{-1}) factors as y ~ N(0,T(K_M|_W)^{-1}) times z ~ N(0,T K_Z^{-1}), so the z-conditional given y is N(0,T K_Z^{-1}) independent of y. Independence from rows: on the fiber {S=M, y} the factor pi_M(p) is constant and cancels. Also verified: loop covector annihilates Z_M (loop.F_M = 0) and the fast common normal (n^+_e+n^+_f)/sqrt2 lies in W_M (dim W_M = 9). The other matching follows by rotation (the model is rotation-invariant, c13:1248-1249).

steps.step: 4. Disintegration chain rule eq:phil-conditioned-parent-chain through C onto the disjoint union of strata of dimensions 9 and 12; H_opt <= kappa_E.
steps.reasoning: C(x,S)=(S,P_{W_S}x) is a deterministic measurable map onto the standard Borel space coprod_S {S} x W_S. lem:prob-kl-chain-rule (c03:261-272) applied to the lifts q(dx,S) delta_{C(x,S)} and mu(dx,S) delta_{C(x,S)}, disintegrated over the C-coordinate, gives KL(q||mu) = KL(C_# q||C_# mu) + int KL(q(.|c)||mu(.|c)) C_#q(dc) in [0,inf] with no absolute-continuity hypothesis; here KL(q_t^E||mu)<=kappa_E<inf so all terms are finite reals. Relative entropy is reference-measure-free, so the different stratum dimensions (9 on matchings, 12 elsewhere) create no normalization issue; the Lebesgue/counting measures mentioned in ca_formation_proofs:1976-1978 only serve to write densities. Off the matchings C is injective, both fiber conditionals are Dirac at the same point, KL = 0. On a matching stratum mu(dz|M,y)=nu_{T,Z} by step 3, so the integral term is exactly H_opt(q_t^E) as defined (line 34-35). Dropping the nonnegative retained term KL(C_#q_t^E||C_#mu) yields eq:phil-conditioned-opt-entropy. No Gaussianity of q_t^E is used.

steps.step: 5a. Physical evaluator kernels as actually defined; the comparison law P-bar_y; its multiplier integrates to one and is retained-measurable.
steps.reasoning: def:rg-formation-experiment (c13:217-219), inherited by the cycle (c13:1206-1207): physical m_i ~ N(mbar_i, sigma^2), k_i | m_i ~ N(m_i, 1-sigma^2), sigma^2=1/2, so k-m ~ N(0,vI), v=1/2, independent of x and m. Recognition (eq:rg-formation-evaluator-lift, c13:224-229): m = mbar + xi, k = kbar + xi + xi', so m has the same law and k-m = Dx + xi' ~ N(Dx, vI), Dx = D y + D F_M z = d_y + d_z. P-bar_y(dz,dU) = Pi_{T,Z}(dz) P_ev(dU|y+F_M z) exp[(d_y.(k-m) - |d_y|^2/2)/v]. For fixed z, under P_ev the increment w=k-m ~ N(0,vI), so E exp(d_y.w/v) = exp(|d_y|^2/(2v)); multiplied by exp(-|d_y|^2/(2v)) this is 1, so P-bar_y is a probability law with z-marginal Pi_{T,Z}, and its U|z conditional is N(dm; mbar(x), sigma^2 I) N(dk-m; d_y, vI) (complete the square: -|w|^2/(2v) + d_y.w/v - |d_y|^2/(2v) = -|w-d_y|^2/(2v)). The multiplier depends only on (y,U), which are retained under the identity extension of C on evaluator samples (c13:1286).

steps.step: 5b. P-bar_y has the physical posterior hidden conditional given (M,y,U); H_phys as defined in the source is what is bounded.
steps.reasoning: Physical posterior on (x,S,U) given the records E=1: the records depend only on (x,S) (c13:1204-1206), so it is Pi_phys(dx,S) P_ev(dU|x) with Pi_phys proportional to pi_S exp(-(V_S + T|x|^2/2)/T) (c13:1210-1212, 'the physical posterior omits the last term'). Its z-conditional given (S=M,y,U) is proportional to Pi_phys(dz|M,y) P_ev(U|y+F_M z); Pi_phys(dz|M,y) = N(0,T(K_Z^phys)^{-1}) with K_Z^phys = diag(8+T,4+T,4+T) because H_M + TI is block diagonal on W (+) Z (sympy, step 3), and pi_M cancels. Under P-bar_y, the z-conditional given U is proportional to Pi_{T,Z}(dz) P_ev(U|y+F_M z) g(y,U), and g cancels; so it equals the physical posterior hidden conditional. H_phys(q) is defined (line 36-39) as the discarded conditional term of the chain rule for KL(q x P_rec || Pi_phys x P_ev) through C-tilde(x,S,U)=(S,P_{W_S}x,U); at a fiber (M,y) that term is int Q_y^U(dU) KL(Q_y(dz|U) || P-bar_y(dz|U)) with Q_y = q(dz|M,y) P_rec(dU|y+F_M z), which is exactly what the proof bounds. Off matchings the fibers are points and the term vanishes.

steps.step: 5c. The chain-rule inequality H_phys(q|M,y) <= KL(q(dz|M,y)||Pi_{T,Z}) + E_q[|d_z|^2/(2v)|M,y].
steps.reasoning: KL(Q_y||P-bar_y) computed z-first: KL(q(dz|M,y)||Pi_{T,Z}) + int q(dz|M,y) KL(P_rec(.|x) || P-bar_y(.|z)); at fixed x=y+F_M z both laws give m ~ N(mbar(x),sigma^2 I), and given m the increment laws are N(d_y+d_z, vI) vs N(d_y, vI), so the inner KL is |d_z|^2/(2v). Computed U-first: KL(Q_y^U||P-bar_y^U) + int Q_y^U(dU) KL(Q_y(dz|U)||P-bar_y(dz|U)) = (nonnegative) + H_phys(q|M,y). Both orders are lem:prob-kl-chain-rule for the same pair; dropping the nonnegative evaluator-marginal term gives the inequality. Q_y << P-bar_y holds (Gaussian kernels of full support, q(dz|M,y) << Pi_{T,Z} for C_#q-a.e. y from q << mu), though the chain rule does not need it.

steps.step: 5d. Tilt identity nu_{T,Z} = Pi_{T,Z} e^{-|d_z|^2/(2v)}/Z_tilt with Z_tilt = (4+T)/(4+5T), and the final bound kappa_E + log((4+5T)/(4+T)) <= kappa_E + T.
steps.reasoning: |d_z|^2/(2v) = z^T F^T D^T D F z /(2v) = z^T F^T R_ev F z / 2 = 2 z_2^2 + 2 z_3^2 (sympy: F^T R_ev F = diag(0,4,4)). Then Pi_{T,Z} e^{-|d_z|^2/(2v)} is proportional to exp(-[(8+T)z_1^2 + ((4+T)+4T) z_2^2 + ((4+T)+4T) z_3^2]/(2T)) = exp(-z^T K_Z z/(2T)), i.e. nu_{T,Z} (sympy: (4+T)/T + 4 = (4+5T)/T). Z_tilt = E_{Pi}[e^{-2 z_2^2 - 2 z_3^2}] = [(1 + 4T/(4+T))^{-1/2}]^2 = (4+T)/(4+5T) (sympy exact). Hence KL(q||Pi) + E_q|d_z|^2/(2v) = E_q log[q/(Pi e^{-|d_z|^2/(2v)})] = KL(q||nu) - log Z_tilt = KL(q||nu) + log((4+5T)/(4+T)), valid since E_q|d_z|^2 < inf (step 6) and KL(q(.|M,y)||nu) is C_#q-integrable (its integral is H_opt <= kappa_E). Integrating over C_#q: H_phys(q_t^E) <= H_opt(q_t^E) + log((4+5T)/(4+T)) C_#q(matchings) <= kappa_E + log((4+5T)/(4+T)). Finally log(1 + 4T/(4+T)) <= 4T/(4+T) <= T (log(1+u)<=u; checked numerically at T=1/100). The statement 'd_y . d_z = 0' (line 145) is true (P_W R_ev P_Z = 0) but is not load-bearing in the argument as written.

steps.step: 6a. Moment and finiteness claims.
steps.reasoning: Native process: initial law N(m_0,I_12) has finite second moment; drift -grad U_S with U_S having Hessian A_S >= TI and diffusion 2TI give L|x|^2 = -2 x^T A_S x + 24T <= -2T|x|^2 + 24T, jumps leave x unchanged (ca_selection_proofs:60-68, eq:phil-selection-moment; the drift does not involve rows so the same bound holds in the learned arm), hence sup_t E|X_t|^2 < inf. Conditioning on E: E[|X|^2 | E] <= E|X|^2 / Pr(E) <= E|X|^2/(1-rho). Gaussian reference log-densities are quadratic in z, so E_q log Pi, E_q log nu, E_q |d_z|^2 are finite; all KL terms are then finite reals (they are also bounded above by kappa_E through the chain rules).

steps.step: 6b. Scaled vs unscaled loss statements (lines 55-59).
steps.reasoning: Scaled negative ELBO is F_T(q) = T KL(q||q*) + const (c13:1244-1246, eq:rg-formation-restricted-vfe) with q* = mu_{T,p(t)} at rows p(t); by thm:rg-exact-coarse-vfe (ii) the discarded part of the scaled free energy is T times H_opt, hence <= T kappa_E. The unscaled physical loss H_phys <= kappa_E + T, and T times it is <= T kappa_E + T^2. These are restatements of the proved bounds.

steps.step: 6c. Limit orders: rho <= 3T + 8 sqrt(2/pi) T^{1/4} + 3408 T^{1/2}; kappa_E = O(T^{1/4} log(1/T)).
steps.reasoning: With delta <= T and a = T^{1/4}: 3 delta <= 3T, 8 sqrt(2/pi) a = 8 sqrt(2/pi) T^{1/4}, 3408 T/a^2 = 3408 T^{1/2}. Along cor:phil-joint-selection the schedule can make both KL(q_t||mu_{T,p(t)}) and TV(q_t,nu_T^M) at most eta_n <= T_n on the window (ca_joint_selection:110-126, 200-204), so eta, delta <= T is attainable. h_b(rho) <= rho log(e/rho): -(1-rho)log(1-rho) <= rho on [0,1] (checked numerically on (0,1/2], max deviation -5e-9). Hence h_b(rho) = O(T^{1/4} log(1/T)), eta = O(T) is lower order, and 1-rho >= 1/2 once rho <= 1/2 (T below ~1.6e-8), giving kappa_E = O(T^{1/4} log(1/T)); numerically kappa_E/(T^{1/4} log(1/T)) is 3.06, 2.01, 1.64 at T = 1e-10, 1e-12, 1e-14.

steps.step: 7. Hidden-sign example (lines 232-243) and its consistency with the bound.
steps.reasoning: Under nu_T^M the hidden coordinate z_1 ~ N(0,T/(8+T)) is independent of the retained state (step 3), so the unconditioned hidden relative entropy is 0. Conditioning on {z_1>0} (probability 1/2) gives density 2 on the half-space and KL = int 2 phi log 2 over {z_1>0} = log 2, independent of T. Consistency: with q = nu_T^M, E = {z_1>0}, r = 1/2, the identity of step 2a reads (1/2)log2 + (1/2)log2 = 0 + I(B;R) = H(B) = log 2, an equality case; the formula (eta+h_b(r))/(1-r) at r=1/2 gives 2 log 2 >= log 2. No contradiction; the example correctly shows the bound cannot vanish unless rho -> 0, and the r=1/2 case lies outside the proposition's rho<1/2 regime anyway. The Dirac remark for full-history conditioning is correct (a point mass is singular to a nondegenerate Gaussian).

steps.step: 8. Statement-vs-proof scope (overclaims, measurability, native vs parent rows).
steps.reasoning: Every displayed inequality (eq:phil-conditioned-full-entropy, -opt-entropy, -physical-entropy) is reconstructed above. The rows-independence clause for the two hidden-conditional bounds follows from pi_S cancelling on fibers (steps 3, 5b), and the restriction of the full-law bound to native rows is correctly stated. No future event is conditioned on, no parent row path is mixed into the reference (rows are the native deterministic p(t)), and no Gaussianity of q_t^E is assumed. The final paragraphs disclaim first-formation and independent-parent conclusions, consistent with the proof. ESTABLISHED status is supported subject to the stated (implicit) rho<1/2 assumption.

steps.step: (1a) J_p is a probability kernel; kappa_S is the p-independent optimizing hidden conditional with drift diag(8+T,4+5T,4+5T)
steps.reasoning: Reconstructed from the model: mu_{T,p}(dx,S) proportional to pi_S(p) exp(-x^T A_S x/(2T)) with A_S=H_S+T(I+R_ev). For a matching M, I verified exactly (sympy, 12x12 matrices built from the residual covectors of def:rg-formation-cycle-experiment) that H_M n^+_g=8n^+_g, H_M n^-_g=4n^-_g, R_ev n^+_g=0, R_ev n^-_g=4n^-_g, that F_M=[(n^+_e-n^+_f)/sqrt2, n^-_e, n^-_f] is orthonormal, and that A_M F_M = F_M diag(8+T,4+5T,4+5T); hence A_M preserves Z_M and W_M=Z_M^perp, x^T A_M x = y^T A_M y + z^T K_Z z, and mu(dx | S=M, P_{W_M}x=y) = N(0,T K_Z^{-1}) in z, independent of y and of pi_M(p) (which cancels). Off the matchings W_S=R^12 and the conditional is a point mass. Integrating kappa_S against sum_{S'} b_p(S'|x)=1 gives total mass one, so J_p is a probability kernel (measurable since kappa_S is an affine Gaussian kernel and b_p is continuous).

steps.step: (1b) Self-proposals leave the state unchanged; projection uses the target W_{S'}; continuous generator is the exact projection; loop covector retained
steps.reasoning: Self-proposal S'=S on a matching: x=y+F_M z with F_M z in Z_M perp W_M, so P_{W_M}x=y; off matchings x=y and P=id. The kernel's atom is delta_{(S',P_{W_{S'}}x)}, i.e. the target's projection, including the 12-dimensional stratum when S' is not a matching. Since A_S preserves W_S, the projected held diffusion dy = -P_{W_S}A_S x dt + sqrt(2T) P_{W_S} dW = -A_S y dt + sqrt(2T) dW^{W_S} is autonomous with generator -A_S y.grad_{W_S} + T Delta_{W_S} (covariance 2T gives T Delta). Loop covector L=sum_i omega_i: I verified L.n^-_g=0, L.n^+_g=-1/sqrt2, hence L.(n^+_e-n^+_f)/sqrt2=0, so L annihilates Z_M (and Z_{M'} by rotation); therefore L lies in every W_S and L.P_{W_{S'}}x = L.x = L.y, so the loop value is preserved exactly across stratum changes, including matching-to-matching jumps.

steps.reasoning: The kinetics redraw S from the product of receiver posterior rows beta_i(j|x)=pi_{ij}e^{-D_{e(i,j)}/T}/sum_{j'}(...) (c13_formation.tex lines 1386-1388; ca_formation_proofs.tex lines 2076-2079). Because V_S=sum_i D_{e(i,S_i)} is additive over receivers and pi_S is a product, prod_i beta_i(S'_i|x) = pi_{S'}e^{-V_{S'}/T}/sum_eta pi_eta e^{-V_eta/T}; and mu_{T,p}(S'|x) = pi_{S'}exp(-x^T A_{S'}x/2T)/sum_eta(...) with the S-independent factor exp(-x^T Omega x/2) cancelling, so the two coincide (this is b_sigma of ca_selection_proofs.tex line 310). Then mu(dx,S)b_p(S'|x)=mu_X(dx)mu(S|x)mu(S'|x) is symmetric in (S,S'). Writing nu=C_# mu, nu(S,dy)kappa_S(dx|y)=mu(S,dx) by disintegration, so nu(d(S,y))J_p((S,y),d(S',y')) is the pushforward of the symmetric measure through (S,x,S') -> ((S,P_{W_S}x),(S',P_{W_{S'}}x)), which commutes with the swap; the pushforward is therefore symmetric on the disjoint union, giving detailed balance and nu J_p = nu without any density or volume factor (the argument is at the level of measures, so 9- and 12-dimensional strata need no separate normalization). Each stratum diffusion is reversible for its Gaussian factor (the W_M-marginal of N(0,T A_M^{-1}) is N(0,T(A_M|_{W_M})^{-1}) because A_M is block diagonal), so the full generator leaves nu invariant.

steps.step: (3a) Second-moment generator bound 25T - 2T|y|^2 (diffusion 24T - 2T|y|^2, hidden draw <= 5T/8)
steps.reasoning: Diffusion part: L|y|^2 = -2 y^T A_S y + 2T dim W_S <= -2T|y|^2 + 24T since A_S >= T I (H_S >= 0, Omega >= I; restriction to W_S keeps the bound) and dim W_S <= 12.
